chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man from the Banu Hashim, who said:

I entered upon a group from the Banu Hashim and greeted them in a dark room. One of them said, 'Greet Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), for he is in the center.' So I greeted him and sat in front of him and said to him, 'I have desired to meet you for a while to ask you about certain things.' He said, 'Ask whatever comes to you.' I said, 'What do you say regarding the bathhouse?' He said, 'Do not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth, and lower your gaze, and do not wash from the used water of the bathhouse, for in it is washed the adulterer, and the son of the adulterer, and the hostile one (Nasibi) towards us, the People of the Household, and he is the worst of them.'

key_terms.الْوَاصِب: The hostile one (specifically towards the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and rulings for entering a bathhouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of modesty (haya) and ritual purity (tahara) in communal spaces, emphasizing that the bathhouse is not merely a place of hygiene but a site of potential spiritual and physical impurity. The Imam’s specific instruction to avoid washing in the 'used water' (ghusalat) reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that residual impurities from fornication and the Nasibi (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) can affect the believer’s ritual state. This guidance underscores the importance of maintaining both external cleanliness and internal spiritual vigilance in public settings.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam,

(It has been narrated) from a man from the Clan of Hashimas who said, ‘I went over to a group from the Clan of Hashimas, so I greeted them in a dark room. So one of them said, ‘Greet Abu Al Hassanasws, for heasws is in the centre’. So I greeted himasws and sat in front of himasws, and I said to himasws, ‘I desired to meet youasws for a while to ask youasws about certain things’. So heasws said: ‘Ask, whatever comes to you’. I said, ‘What are youasws saying regarding the bathhouse’. Heasws said: ‘Do not enter the bathhouse except with a loincloth, and lowering your eyes, and do not wash from the used water of the bathhouse for there has washed in it the adulterer, and the son of the adulterer, and the Hostile one (Nasibi) towards usasws, the Peopleasws of the Household, and he is the most evil of them’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once entered a bathhouse with abu Basir and saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who had applied (lime) and on his underarms.

I then informed abu Basir and he asked me to lead him so he can ask him about it. I said, ‘I saw him.’ He said, ‘You saw him (the Imam) but I cannot see him (the Imam)? Lead me to where he is.’ I then led him and he said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, my lead has said that you have applied lime and on your underarms.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, O abu Muhammad, pulling up hairs of underarms weakens eyesight, so you must apply lime, O abu Muhammad.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I applied since that time and he (the Imam) said, ‘Apply; it is cleansing.’”
